content: Niʿmat Allāh was a popularizer of Akbarian mystical theory and one of the most prominent Sufi lettrists of his day, Qāsim-i Anvār a promoter of Ibn ʿArabī in poetry and preaching; Melvin-Koushki says that, though not a professional Sufi, Ibn Turka's intellectual programme gave him common cause with these masters.
